answer: View each new agent through the prism of a memory-hard proof of work: require a fresh, unpredictable puzzle before admission and expire unused solutions. Every identity then consumes RAM, electricity and time, making a grove of fake accounts costly to grow. Frequent renewal keeps that cost alive like an ember. The limit is unequal hardware: wealthy attackers can still buy many identities, while honest users on weak devices pay a disproportionate price.
